title: 91. Numeracy & Number Systems: Distinguishing Exact and Approximate Numeric Results
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Exact Counted Values Versus Approximate Measured Values
questions.learningObjective: Identify whether a given numeric result is exact or approximate based on its source.
questions.question: Which of the following is an exact numeric result?

options.label: A
options.text: The height of a student measured to the nearest centimetre

options.label: B
options.text: The number of students present in a classroom

questions.explanation: Counting the students present gives a definite whole-number value; no measurement or rounding is involved, so it is exact. A height measured to the nearest centimetre is obtained by measurement and rounding, so it is approximate.
questions.hint: Ask whether the value comes from counting or from measuring.

questions.concept: Exact Arithmetic Versus Approximate Measurement Calculation
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish an approximate result from an exact arithmetic result.
questions.question: Which result is approximate?

options.label: B
options.text: The area of a rectangle calculated from side lengths measured to the nearest centimetre

questions.explanation: The side lengths used to calculate the area are measured values, so they already contain rounding uncertainty. The calculated area is therefore approximate. The sum \(3+5=8\) is obtained from exact numbers and is exact.
questions.hint: Consider whether the numbers entering the calculation are measured or exact.

questions.learningObjective: Recognize that a rounded decimal is an approximate representation of the original number.
questions.question: Which statement is correct for the number \(7.38\) rounded to \(1\) decimal place?
questions.explanation: Rounding \(7.38\) to \(1\) decimal place gives \(7.4\), but this rounded value is not exactly equal to \(7.38\). The symbol \({\approx}\) correctly indicates an approximate equality.
questions.hint: Round the number to one decimal place, then compare the rounded value with the original digit by digit.

questions.concept: Approximate Decimal Expansion of a Repeating Fraction
questions.learningObjective: Determine whether a written decimal expansion of a fraction is exact or approximate.
questions.question: A student writes \(10 \div 3 = 3.33\). Which statement is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: \(3.33\) is approximate because \(10 \div 3\) has a repeating decimal expansion.

options.label: B
options.text: \(3.33\) is exact because it is written as a decimal.

questions.explanation: The exact value of \(10 \div 3\) is the repeating decimal \(3.333\ldots\), not \(3.33\). Writing \(3.33\) truncates the decimal expansion after two decimal places, so it is an approximate value.
questions.hint: Check whether the decimal expansion terminates exactly or continues indefinitely.

questions.concept: Exact Symbolic Representation Versus Decimal Approximation
questions.learningObjective: Identify an exact representation of a well-known irrational number.
questions.question: Which is an exact representation of the number \(\pi\)?
questions.explanation: The symbol \(\pi\) represents the exact value of the constant. The decimal \(3.14\) is a rounded approximation to two decimal places and is not exactly equal to \(\pi\).
questions.hint: An exact representation need not be written as a finite decimal.

questions.learningObjective: Determine whether a reported measurement is exact or approximate.
questions.question: A length is obtained by measurement and reported as \(12.0\text{ cm}\). Which statement is correct?

options.label: B
options.text: The length is approximate because it is a measurement.

questions.explanation: The value \(12.0\text{ cm}\) comes from a measurement, so it has limited precision and includes measurement uncertainty. Even though it is written with one decimal place, it is not an exact value.
questions.hint: Consider whether the value was obtained by measuring rather than by counting or exact definition.

questions.learningObjective: Determine when a calculation result remains exact.
questions.question: A well-defined calculation uses only exact counts and exact fractions, and no rounding is applied. The result should be regarded as:
questions.explanation: Exact counts and exact fractions are exact inputs. If the calculation is performed without rounding or approximation, the result remains exact. The presence of fractions alone does not make a result approximate.
questions.hint: Focus on whether any input or step introduces rounding.

questions.concept: Exact Fraction Addition Versus Decimal Approximation
questions.learningObjective: Determine which computation gives an exact result.
questions.question: Which computation gives an exact result?
questions.explanation: The sum \(\frac{2}{5}+\frac{1}{5}=\frac{3}{5}\) is exact because it uses exact fractions and no rounding. The statement \(\frac{1}{3}\approx 0.333\) uses an approximate decimal value.
questions.hint: Look for calculations that do not use rounded decimal values.

questions.learningObjective: Compare a calculation from an approximate input with the exact calculation.
questions.question: A student substitutes \(0.142857\) for \(\frac{1}{7}\) and multiplies it by \(7\). Which statement correctly compares this result with \(7\times\frac{1}{7}\)?

options.label: B
options.text: The substituted calculation gives \(0.999999\), an approximation to the exact result \(1\).

questions.explanation: The finite decimal gives \(7\times0.142857=0.999999\), whereas \(7\times\left(\frac{1}{7}\right)=1\). The truncated input produces a nonzero difference in this specific calculation. The alternative incorrectly treats the substituted input as equal to \(\frac{1}{7}\).
questions.hint: Multiply the stated finite decimal exactly, then compare with the fraction calculation.

questions.concept: Definition of Exact and Approximate Numeric Results
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish exact results from approximate results by the presence or absence of rounding error.
questions.question: Which statement best distinguishes exact numeric results from approximate numeric results?

options.label: A
options.text: An exact result equals the true value; an approximate result comes from limited precision, rounding, truncation, or measurement uncertainty.

options.label: B
options.text: Any result written with a decimal point is exact.

questions.explanation: An exact result represents the true value without rounding or measurement uncertainty. An approximate result arises from rounding, measurement, or truncation and may therefore contain error. Writing a decimal point does not by itself make a result exact.
questions.hint: Compare whether the result represents the true value without any rounding or uncertainty.
